poster_title: Teaching Language Models to Critique via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zhihui Xie, Jie Chen, Liyu Chen, Weichao Mao, Jingjing Xu, Lingpeng Kong
paper_info: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada, 2025

panels.headline: Recent advances in LLMs show potential for self-improvement through feedback mechanisms, but without proper guidance, these loops can degrade performance.
content: LLMs can critique and refine their outputs.
Current feedback mechanisms lack actionable guidance.
Reward models and verification tools are insufficient.
CTRL aims to provide targeted and actionable feedback.
Decoupling critic and task-performing models allows for generalization.

panels.headline: Two-stage pipeline: (1) supervised finetuning with high-quality critiques, (2) Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
content: Decouples critic from task-performing model.
Uses execution feedback for supervised finetuning.
Optimizes critic through GRPO.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of our two-stage training pipeline CTRL.

panels.headline: Evaluated on CodeContests, LiveCodeBench, MBPP+, and JudgeBench.
content: Conducted extensive evaluations on diverse benchmarks.
Simulated different levels of critiquing and discrimination abilities.
Compared performance across various benchmarks and models.
panels.figure_caption: Performance scaling of our CTRL critic compared to other critics across different generators on CodeContests.

panels.headline: Achieved up to 106.1% relative improvement on CodeContests with base model and up to 23.5% with stronger model.
content: CTRL significantly enhances pass rates and mitigates compounding errors.
Reduced revision iterations, leading to lower token consumption.
Demonstrated strong critiquing capabilities across different generators.
panels.figure_caption: Simulation results showing success probability as a function of the number of attempts, comparing different levels of critiquing and discrimination ability.

panels.headline: Relatively weaker critic models can effectively guide stronger task-performing models, showcasing a weak-to-strong generalization phenomenon.
content: CTRL outperforms self-critique methods and approaches using stronger critics.
Enabled efficient test-time scaling through iterative critique-revisions.
Showed significant improvements in performance and efficiency.
Reduced the number of revision iterations needed.
Lower token consumption and higher success rates.

panels.headline: CTRL is a promising framework for training critic LLMs to provide actionable feedback for code generation, leading to significant improvements in performance and efficiency.
content: CTRL provides actionable feedback for code generation.
Significantly improves performance and efficiency.
Decoupling critic and task-performing models allows for generalization.
Future work includes exploring more complex refinement processes.
Potential applications in other domains beyond code generation.
